mostWorthwhile.text: Filling the vessel circuit was most worthwhile: the exchange inset showed oxygen and nutrients leaving the capillary, carbon dioxide returning, and red cells staying inside. That connected the blood’s ingredients to their role in supplying tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: Trying to connect the heart to the empty vessel circuit was confusing. The result said the heart could not combine with anything, but did not explain that blood had to be added first.

surprise.text: I was interested that these red blood cells have neither a nucleus nor mitochondria but still make ATP from sugar in their fluid. That contrasted with the muscle cells described earlier.

arbitrary.text: The required order for connecting the heart felt somewhat arbitrary: the parts suggested a circuit, but the failed attempt did not explain why the heart had to wait until the vessels contained blood.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, because assembling circulation and seeing where exchange happens helped connect cellular needs to a body system. I would hope later combinations explain their ordering when it is not apparent.
